assessmentSummary.identity: A submaximal or high-intent countermovement box jump used to coordinate the backward arm load with the countermovement and the upward arm drive with lower-body propulsion.
currentCardFindings: The movement is a technique emphasis within a standard arm-swing box jump, not a distinct external task.
Arm timing needs an observable temporal criterion instead of generic advice to coordinate the sequence.
The 50-point score omits physical demand, supervision, collision consequence, impact, and fatigue while all controlled support fields are empty.

proposedDosage.timingTarget: arms finish the backward load with the lowest center-of-mass position and reverse upward before takeoff
proposedDosage.progressWhen: arm and leg reversals are synchronized without a pause, double dip, or late reach

athleteInstructions: Let the arms load with the hips
Swing up as you drive off the floor

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Consolidate with Box Jump after human identity review. Preserve arm-swing timing as a technique annotation or movement-intelligence delivery profile; natural arm swing remains the baseline.

currentCardSnapshot.description: Arm-Swing Timing Box Jump is a technical box-jump skill drill. The athlete moves at a teachable speed, coordinates the takeoff and landing sequence, and resets every rep so the pattern stays crisp. It prepares the athlete for higher-intent box jumps without turning the set into conditioning.

evidence.sourceTitle: Basics of Strength and Conditioning Manual
claims: A box-jump identity must specify start condition, countermovement permission, arm use, takeoff and landing laterality, approach, platform relationship, stabilization, exit, and reset behavior.
Arm-Swing Timing Box Jump must not combine a floor-to-box jump with a depth or drop jump, repeated rebound, box jump-over, unilateral landing, seated start, approach jump, or loaded jump.
A reset box jump is a discrete ballistic propulsion task followed by an elevated landing and deliberate stabilization; repeated reactive box contacts are a different task.
Arm-Swing Timing Box Jump belongs to bilateral vertical power and landing control, with start condition, arm use, box height, landing strategy, and reset intent encoded as controlled dimensions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Basics of Strength and Conditioning Manual
claims: Propulsion and elevated landing are coordinated across the foot, ankle, knee, hip, pelvis, trunk, and, when permitted, the shoulder girdle.

The card should assign propulsion to the plantar flexors, quadriceps, and hip extensors; stabilization to the foot, hip, and trunk stabilizers; and arm-swing contribution to coordinated shoulder flexion without claiming one isolated prime mover.

evidence.sourceTitle: Does Box Height Matter? A Comparative Analysis of Box Height on Box Jump Performance in Men and Women
claims: In recreationally active adults asked to jump maximally, changing box height across the studied range generally did not change most propulsive performance variables.

Box height is therefore a landing target and constraint, not a valid stand-alone measure of vertical jump height; observable quality includes maximal intent when prescribed, full-foot clearance, quiet simultaneous contact, controlled landing depth, and a stable finish.

evidence.sourceTitle: Basics of Strength and Conditioning Manual
claims: Box-jump difficulty changes with required impulse, box collision consequence, landing-space tolerance, start condition, arm restriction, laterality, approach, external load, repetition strategy, and fatigue.

Exercise cards must score technical complexity, physical or absolute-load demand, coordination, supervision, failure consequence, impact, work-capacity demand, and overall difficulty directly; they must not use skill-library levels.
Jump volume is counted as discrete takeoffs and landings, while height, intent, start condition, arm use, body mass, external load, and reset duration govern exposure.

Arm-Swing Timing Box Jump needs contact count, output intent, impact and eccentric stress, technical-fatigue criteria, and recovery guidance; a reset power prescription must not be converted into a conditioning interval.

evidence.sourceTitle: Does Box Height Matter? A Comparative Analysis of Box Height on Box Jump Performance in Men and Women
claims: Different box heights can be used without assuming that a higher box produces a better propulsive effort, provided the athlete can clear and land on the platform safely.

The delivery profile should require a stable non-slip platform, unobstructed takeoff and top surfaces, adequate ceiling and forward clearance, a safe step-down route, athlete-specific height selection, and coach sightlines to the feet and landing.
Power-focused plyometrics use low-repetition sets, deliberate resets, and enough recovery to preserve takeoff output and landing quality.
Prescribe sets, discrete repetitions, box-height selection rule, landing hold, step-down behavior, rest, and stop criteria; do not prescribe maximal box height as the training target.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Specific external or movement-focused feedback can improve landing mechanics, while excessive cue volume can impair learning.
Use a small cue set: choose an honest box, load and drive, clear the front edge, land quietly with the whole foot, own the top, stand, step down, and reset.

evidence.sourceTitle: Basics of Strength and Conditioning Manual
claims: Box-jump hazards include collision with the front edge, missed or partial foot contact, unstable or shifting equipment, uncontrolled landing, and an unsafe jump-down exit.

Stop for pain, giving way, hesitation, repeated toe catch, partial-foot landing, excessive hip tuck used to chase box height, loud or asymmetrical contact, valgus or trunk collapse, loss of output, or any platform movement.

evidence.sourceTitle: Does Box Height Matter? A Comparative Analysis of Box Height on Box Jump Performance in Men and Women
claims: Box height should be selected to support the intended landing or teaching goal rather than used as a proxy for jump performance.

Arm-Swing Timing Box Jump belongs early in an output block after readiness work, or in movement intelligence when explicitly submaximal and technique-focused; low volume and full reset preserve the intended stimulus.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Use of Augmented Information for Reducing Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury Risk During Jump Landings: A Systematic Review
claims: Athlete support should show the prescribed start, target box, landing shape, hold, stand, step-down route, and one primary cue.
The interface should explain that a higher box can reward extra hip flexion without proving a higher jump and should display a lower-box or non-box regression without shame language.

evidence.sourceTitle: Does Box Height Matter? A Comparative Analysis of Box Height on Box Jump Performance in Men and Women
claims: Coaches can change box height for teaching and landing purposes without treating box height as the propulsive outcome.

Coach support should provide side and front observation, edge-clearance and full-foot criteria, landing-depth comparison, collision-risk rules, output and contact counting, regressions, progressions, and a prohibition on jumping down during reset prescriptions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Exercise selection and progression should match physical and psychosocial readiness, technical competence, supervision, and equipment scale.

Accessibility can be improved with a lower soft-surface platform, visible takeoff line, contrasting box edge, landing footprint marks, demonstrated step-down route, longer reset, or a vertical jump-to-stick regression without assigning an exercise skill level.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Difference Between Countermovement and Squat Jump Performances: A Review of Underlying Mechanisms With Practical Applications
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: A countermovement jump and a static squat jump have different start mechanics and performance characteristics, so start condition must be explicit.

Box height and landing hold are usually delivery modifiers; a static start, arm restriction, seated start, approach, unilateral landing, external load, or prior drop changes the exercise sufficiently to require a controlled variant or separate definition.
